answer: To hold back a tide of fake agents, let established members sponsor newcomers from a fixed, nonrenewable invitation budget. Each sponsorship locks collateral until the newcomer completes randomly audited jobs; proven collusion burns both bonds. The audit is a lantern on fabricated work, while scarce invitations form a ridge against mass entry. Attackers must buy sponsors and risk capital. A captured founding group can still admit its own swarm, and honest newcomers may struggle to find sponsors.
